claim: The primary cilium is nucleated by the mother centriole-derived basal body.
source: The primary cilium is nucleated by the mother centriole-derived basal body (BB) via as yet poorly characterized mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge in the field.

claim: BBs have been reported to degenerate following ciliogenesis in the C. elegans embryo.
source: BBs have been reported to degenerate following ciliogenesis in the C. elegans embryo, although neither BB architecture nor early ciliogenesis steps have been described in this organism.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and references prior reports.

claim: Neither BB architecture nor early ciliogenesis steps have been described in C. elegans.
source: BBs have been reported to degenerate following ciliogenesis in the C. elegans embryo, although neither BB architecture nor early ciliogenesis steps have been described in this organism.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Doroquez et al., 2014 described the three-dimensional morphologies of sensory neuron cilia in adult C. elegans hermaphrodites at high resolution.
source: In a previous study (Doroquez et al., 2014), we described the three-dimensional morphologies of sensory neuron cilia in adult C. elegans hermaphrodites at high resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract with a citation to prior work.

claim: BBs remodel to support ciliogenesis in a subset of sensory neurons in C. elegans.
source: Here, we use serial section electron microscopy and tomography of staged C. elegans embryos to demonstrate that BBs remodel to support ciliogenesis in a subset of sensory neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Centriolar singlet microtubules are converted into BB doublets in C. elegans sensory neurons.
source: We show that centriolar singlet microtubules are converted into BB doublets which subsequently grow asynchronously to template the ciliary axoneme, visualize degeneration of the centriole core, and define the developmental stage at which the transition zone is established.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: BB doublets grow asynchronously to template the ciliary axoneme in C. elegans sensory neurons.
source: We show that centriolar singlet microtubules are converted into BB doublets which subsequently grow asynchronously to template the ciliary axoneme, visualize degeneration of the centriole core, and define the developmental stage at which the transition zone is established.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The centriole core degenerates during ciliogenesis in C. elegans sensory neurons.
source: We show that centriolar singlet microtubules are converted into BB doublets which subsequently grow asynchronously to template the ciliary axoneme, visualize degeneration of the centriole core, and define the developmental stage at which the transition zone is established.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 2.

claim: The developmental stage at which the transition zone is established has been defined.
source: We show that centriolar singlet microtubules are converted into BB doublets which subsequently grow asynchronously to template the ciliary axoneme, visualize degeneration of the centriole core, and define the developmental stage at which the transition zone is established.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 2.

claim: Cilia play key roles in regulating embryonic development, sensory signaling, and motility.
source: Cilia are evolutionarily conserved microtubule (MT)-based organelles that play key roles in regulating embryonic development, sensory signaling, and motility among other cellular functions (Goetz and Anderson, 2010; Green and Mykytyn, 2010; Yildiz and Khanna, 2012; Falk et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations to support the claim.

claim: Both immotile primary and motile cilia are nucleated by a basal body that is generally derived from the mother centriole.
source: Both immotile primary and motile cilia are nucleated by a basal body (BB) that is generally derived from the mother centriole (Marshall, 2007; Kim and Dynlacht, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: BBs possess accessory structures such as transition fibers that associate with a ciliary vesicle or dock with the plasma membrane.
source: BBs possess accessory structures such as transition fibers that associate with a ciliary vesicle or dock with the plasma membrane and provide a platform for assembly of intraflagellar transport (IFT) complexes that are essential for elongation of the ciliary axoneme (Kim and Dynlacht, 2013; Azimzadeh and Marshall, 2010; Reiter et al., 2012; Dawe et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Transition fibers provide a platform for assembly of intraflagellar transport (IFT) complexes that are essential for elongation of the ciliary axoneme.
source: BBs possess accessory structures such as transition fibers that associate with a ciliary vesicle or dock with the plasma membrane and provide a platform for assembly of intraflagellar transport (IFT) complexes that are essential for elongation of the ciliary axoneme (Kim and Dynlacht, 2013; Azimzadeh and Marshall, 2010; Reiter et al., 2012; Dawe et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Overall organization of centrioles/BBs, as well as many proteins required for their assembly and function are conserved.
source: Although overall organization of centrioles/BBs, as well as many proteins required for their assembly and function are conserved, ultrastructural features of these cellular structures can differ among and within species.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Ultrastructural features of centrioles/BBs can differ among and within species.
source: Although overall organization of centrioles/BBs, as well as many proteins required for their assembly and function are conserved, ultrastructural features of these cellular structures can differ among and within species.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Centrioles/BBs are cylindrical structures that can be comprised of a radially symmetric array of MT singlets, doublets, or triplets depending on the species and cellular context.
source: For instance, centrioles/BBs are cylindrical structures that can be comprised of a radially symmetric array of MT singlets, doublets, or triplets depending on the species and cellular context (Azimzadeh and Marshall, 2010; Winey and O'Toole, 2014; Carvalho-Santos et al., 2011; Gottardo et al., 2015; González et al., 1998; Jana et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: It remains unclear whether centrioles of distinct ultrastructural organization transition to BBs and nucleate cilia via similar or distinct mechanisms.
source: It remains unclear whether centrioles of distinct ultrastructural organization transition to BBs and nucleate cilia via similar or distinct mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Centrioles in one-cell C. elegans embryos are structurally distinct from their mammalian counterparts.
source: Ultrastructural analyses of centrioles in one-cell C. elegans embryos have shown that centrioles in this organism are structurally distinct from their mammalian counterparts (Pelletier et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: C. elegans centrioles are relatively small compared to those in mammals.
source: C. elegans centrioles are relatively small compared to those in mammals and are comprised of a central tube surrounded by nine singlet MTs (sMTs), as compared to the cartwheel structure surrounded by triplet MTs found in larger mammalian centrioles (Winey and O'Toole, 2014; Pelletier et al., 2006; Hilbert et al., 2013; Gönczy, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: C. elegans centrioles are comprised of a central tube surrounded by nine singlet MTs.
source: C. elegans centrioles are relatively small compared to those in mammals and are comprised of a central tube surrounded by nine singlet MTs (sMTs), as compared to the cartwheel structure surrounded by triplet MTs found in larger mammalian centrioles (Winey and O'Toole, 2014; Pelletier et al., 2006; Hilbert et al., 2013; Gönczy, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Mammalian centrioles have a cartwheel structure surrounded by triplet MTs.
source: C. elegans centrioles are relatively small compared to those in mammals and are comprised of a central tube surrounded by nine singlet MTs (sMTs), as compared to the cartwheel structure surrounded by triplet MTs found in larger mammalian centrioles (Winey and O'Toole, 2014; Pelletier et al., 2006; Hilbert et al., 2013; Gönczy, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: C. elegans and vertebrate centrioles are built using subsets of conserved proteins.
source: Despite these differences, C. elegans and vertebrate centrioles are built using subsets of conserved proteins (Carvalho-Santos et al., 2011; Gönczy, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Primary cilia are present only on sensory neurons in C. elegans.
source: Primary cilia are present only on sensory neurons in C. elegans (Ward et al., 1975; Perkins et al., 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Cilia in C. elegans are templated by BBs derived from centrioles.
source: As in other organisms, these cilia are templated by BBs derived from centrioles (Perkins et al., 1986).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: BBs in C. elegans have been reported to degenerate following cilia assembly in the embryo.
source: However, BBs in C. elegans have been reported to degenerate following cilia assembly in the embryo, and no canonical BB structures or core centriolar components are detected in ciliated neurons in wild-type animals at postembryonic stages (Perkins et al., 1986; Dammermann et al., 2009; Schouteden et al., 2015; Doroquez et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: No canonical BB structures or core centriolar components are detected in ciliated neurons in wild-type C. elegans animals at postembryonic stages.
source: However, BBs in C. elegans have been reported to degenerate following cilia assembly in the embryo, and no canonical BB structures or core centriolar components are detected in ciliated neurons in wild-type animals at postembryonic stages (Perkins et al., 1986; Dammermann et al., 2009; Schouteden et al., 2015; Doroquez et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: A subset of BB-associated proteins remains enriched at the cilia base in adult C. elegans animals.
source: Intriguingly, despite this apparent degeneration, a subset of BB-associated proteins remains enriched at the cilia base in adult animals as shown via immunofluorescence (Dammermann et al., 2009; Mohan et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2013, 2016), suggesting the presence of centriolar/BB 'remnants'.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The presence of BB-associated proteins at the cilia base in adult C. elegans suggests the presence of centriolar/BB 'remnants'.
source: Intriguingly, despite this apparent degeneration, a subset of BB-associated proteins remains enriched at the cilia base in adult animals as shown via immunofluorescence (Dammermann et al., 2009; Mohan et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2013, 2016), suggesting the presence of centriolar/BB 'remnants'.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from the cited data.

claim: Sensory neurons in C. elegans are born and differentiate at late embryonic stages.
source: Since sensory neurons are born and differentiate at late embryonic stages (Sulston et al., 1983) that are technically challenging to analyze experimentally, key early steps in ciliogenesis including the centriole-to-BB transition, the precise timing of centriolar degeneration, and initiation of axoneme elongation, have yet to be examined in this organism.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Key early steps in ciliogenesis including the centriole-to-BB transition, the precise timing of centriolar degeneration, and initiation of axoneme elongation, have yet to be examined in C. elegans.
source: Since sensory neurons are born and differentiate at late embryonic stages (Sulston et al., 1983) that are technically challenging to analyze experimentally, key early steps in ciliogenesis including the centriole-to-BB transition, the precise timing of centriolar degeneration, and initiation of axoneme elongation, have yet to be examined in this organism.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge.

claim: The average diameter of centrioles at 350 mpf is 88.2 ± 4.2 nm.
source: The average diameter and length of centrioles at this developmental stage were 88.2 ± 4.2 nm and 100.7 ± 0.2 nm, respectively (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a measurement reported in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: The average length of centrioles at 350 mpf is 100.7 ± 0.2 nm.
source: The average diameter and length of centrioles at this developmental stage were 88.2 ± 4.2 nm and 100.7 ± 0.2 nm, respectively (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a measurement reported in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: Bilateral amphid channels containing sensory neuron endings were readily visible at the bean stage and all subsequent stages.
source: In contrast to our observations at 350 mpf, bilateral amphid channels containing sensory neuron endings were readily visible at this and all subsequent stages (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in the figures.

claim: Centrioles at the bean stage were not located in close proximity to the cell surface and dendritic tip but were instead found deep within the cell.
source: Centrioles in this stage were not located in close proximity to the cell surface and dendritic tip but were instead found deep within the cell (Figure 1Ci and iv).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1.

claim: At the bean stage, a transition from sMTs with hooks to dMTs was observed in centrioles.
source: Interestingly, at this stage, we observed a transition from sMTs with hooks to dMTs. Specifically, centrioles in several amphid neurons were comprised of the central tube surrounded by a mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks (Figure 1Cii–iii).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1.

claim: Centrioles at the bean stage were comprised of the central tube surrounded by a mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks.
source: Specifically, centrioles in several amphid neurons were comprised of the central tube surrounded by a mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks (Figure 1Cii–iii).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1.

claim: The average length of centrioles at the bean stage was similar to that at the 350 mpf stage.
source: The average length of these structures at the bean stage was similar to that at the 350 mpf stage (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a comparison reported in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: sMTs remodel to form dMTs by closure of the A tubule-associated hooks to generate B-tubules.
source: We, therefore, infer that sMTs remodel to form dMTs by closure of the A tubule-associated hooks to generate B-tubules.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the observed transition from sMTs with hooks to dMTs.

claim: The transition from sMTs to dMTs likely occurs asynchronously within a centriole.
source: As these centrioles contain both dMTs and sMTs with hooks within the same 70 nm section, the transition from sMTs to dMTs likely occurs asynchronously within a centriole.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the observation of mixed sMTs and dMTs within the same section.

claim: Centriole remodeling is initiated by the bean stage of embryonic development in a subset of amphid sensory neurons.
source: We henceforth refer to this remodeled structure as the BB, and conclude that this remodeling is initiated by the bean stage of embryonic development in a subset of amphid sensory neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the observed structural changes.

claim: By the comma stage, BBs in a subset of amphid neurons were found in close proximity to the cell surface.
source: By the 'comma' stage (Figure 1A), BBs in a subset of amphid neurons were found in close proximity to the cell surface (Figure 1Di and iv).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1.

claim: The average length of BBs at the comma stage was mildly increased compared to the bean stage.
source: Although the average length of these structures was mildly increased, their mean diameter and length were not significantly different relative to those at the bean stage (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is a comparison reported in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: The mean diameter and length of BBs at the comma stage were not significantly different relative to those at the bean stage.
source: Although the average length of these structures was mildly increased, their mean diameter and length were not significantly different relative to those at the bean stage (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is a comparison reported in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: At the comma stage, dMTs surrounded the central tube in the most proximal BB regions.
source: At the comma stage, dMTs surrounded the central tube in the most proximal BB regions; however, a mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks was present in more distal BB/axoneme regions in most examined cells (Figure 1Dii–iii).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1.

claim: At the comma stage, a mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks was present in more distal BB/axoneme regions in most examined cells.
source: At the comma stage, dMTs surrounded the central tube in the most proximal BB regions; however, a mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks was present in more distal BB/axoneme regions in most examined cells (Figure 1Dii–iii).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1.

claim: As BBs/axonemes elongate in later stage embryos, only dMTs were detected in proximal regions.
source: As BBs/axonemes elongate in later stage embryos (Figure 2A–C, Figure 3B), only dMTs were detected in proximal regions, whereas a mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks were present in more distal regions of axonemes in 1.5- and two-fold embryos (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: A mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks were present in more distal regions of axonemes in 1.5- and two-fold embryos.
source: As BBs/axonemes elongate in later stage embryos (Figure 2A–C, Figure 3B), only dMTs were detected in proximal regions, whereas a mixture of dMTs and sMTs with hooks were present in more distal regions of axonemes in 1.5- and two-fold embryos (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2.

claim: A- and B-tubules of BBs/axonemes grow asynchronously in examined amphid sensory neurons.
source: These observations suggest that A- and B-tubules of BBs/axonemes grow asynchronously in examined amphid sensory neurons (summarized in Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the observed mixture of dMTs and sMTs at different stages, and is summarized in Figure 3C.

claim: The diameter of the proximal BB/axoneme region was variable at the 1.5-fold stage.
source: We found that in embryos, the diameter of the proximal BB/axoneme region was variable at the 1.5-fold stage and significantly increased by the two-fold stage (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: The diameter of the proximal BB/axoneme region significantly increased by the two-fold stage.
source: We found that in embryos, the diameter of the proximal BB/axoneme region was variable at the 1.5-fold stage and significantly increased by the two-fold stage (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: Core centriolar/BB markers such as SAS-4 are lost by the two-fold stage by immunofluorescence.
source: Previous observations have reported loss of core centriolar/BB markers such as SAS-4 by the two-fold stage by immunofluorescence (Dammermann et al., 2009; Schouteden et al., 2015), raising the possibility that the increased BB diameter is a consequence of degeneration of core centriolar structures.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The increased BB diameter is possibly a consequence of degeneration of core centriolar structures.
source: Previous observations have reported loss of core centriolar/BB markers such as SAS-4 by the two-fold stage by immunofluorescence (Dammermann et al., 2009; Schouteden et al., 2015), raising the possibility that the increased BB diameter is a consequence of degeneration of core centriolar structures.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the Results section based on prior observations and current data.

claim: All examined cross-sections of centrioles/BBs in 350 mpf embryos as well as bean and comma-stage amphid neurons contained the central tube.
source: All examined cross-sections of centrioles/BBs in 350 mpf embryos as well as bean and comma-stage amphid neurons contained the central tube with an average diameter of 60.9 ± 4.2 nm (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1.

claim: The average diameter of the central tube is 60.9 ± 4.2 nm.
source: All examined cross-sections of centrioles/BBs in 350 mpf embryos as well as bean and comma-stage amphid neurons contained the central tube with an average diameter of 60.9 ± 4.2 nm (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is a measurement reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1.

claim: The central tube appeared to be present in only a subset of examined BBs in 1.5-fold embryos.
source: However, the central tube appeared to be present in only a subset of examined BBs in 1.5-fold embryos (compare Figure 2Aiv with Figure 2Av, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) and was absent from all examined BBs in two- and three-fold embryos (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2.

claim: The central tube was absent from all examined BBs in two- and three-fold embryos.
source: However, the central tube appeared to be present in only a subset of examined BBs in 1.5-fold embryos (compare Figure 2Aiv with Figure 2Av, Figure 2—figure supplement 2) and was absent from all examined BBs in two- and three-fold embryos (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2.

claim: The diameter of the proximal regions of BBs with seemingly degenerated central tubes was larger than that of BBs with intact central tubes.
source: The diameter of the proximal regions of BBs with seemingly degenerated central tubes was larger than that of BBs with intact central tubes (compare Figure 2Av with Figure 2Aiv, Figure 2Bv and Cv).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2.

claim: Flaring of dMTs at the ciliary base was observed in longitudinal sections in a subset of amphid neurons at the 1.5-fold stage.
source: Consistent with a significant increase in proximal BB/axoneme diameter evident from cross-sections, we observed flaring of dMTs at the ciliary base in longitudinal sections in a subset of amphid neurons at the 1.5-fold stage (Figure 2Ai and Avii), and in all examined amphid neurons at the two- and three-fold embryonic stages (Figure 2Bi, Bvi, 3Ci and Cvi).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2.

claim: Flaring of dMTs at the ciliary base was observed in all examined amphid neurons at the two- and three-fold embryonic stages.
source: Consistent with a significant increase in proximal BB/axoneme diameter evident from cross-sections, we observed flaring of dMTs at the ciliary base in longitudinal sections in a subset of amphid neurons at the 1.5-fold stage (Figure 2Ai and Avii), and in all examined amphid neurons at the two- and three-fold embryonic stages (Figure 2Bi, Bvi, 3Ci and Cvi).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Central tubes degenerate asynchronously in individual amphid neurons.
source: These results suggest that central tubes degenerate asynchronously in individual amphid neurons, and that degeneration of the central tube starting at the 1.5-fold stage likely accounts for the flaring of BB dMT arrays and increased BB diameters (Figure 3A and C).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the observed variability in central tube presence at the 1.5-fold stage.

claim: Degeneration of the central tube starting at the 1.5-fold stage likely accounts for the flaring of BB dMT arrays and increased BB diameters.
source: These results suggest that central tubes degenerate asynchronously in individual amphid neurons, and that degeneration of the central tube starting at the 1.5-fold stage likely accounts for the flaring of BB dMT arrays and increased BB diameters (Figure 3A and C).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the correlation between central tube loss and increased BB diameter.

claim: No obvious structures resembling transition fibers were detected associated with BBs in C. elegans amphid neurons at any developmental stage by TEM of HPF-FS samples.
source: As we reported previously (Doroquez et al., 2014), we did not detect any obvious structures resembling transition fibers associated with BBs in C. elegans amphid neurons at any developmental stage by TEM of HPF-FS samples.
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section with a citation to prior work.

claim: The TZ at the cilia base is the proximal-most compartment of the axoneme proper.
source: The TZ at the cilia base is the proximal-most compartment of the axoneme proper.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as established knowledge.

claim: The TZ is defined ultrastructurally by the presence of proteinacious Y-links that originate at the outer junction between A- and B-tubules of axonemal dMTs, and project toward and usually connect to the plasma membrane.
source: This compartment is defined ultrastructurally by the presence of proteinacious Y-links that originate at the outer junction between A- and B-tubules of axonemal dMTs, and project toward and usually connect to the plasma membrane (Reiter et al., 2012; Blacque and Sanders, 2014; Czarnecki and Shah, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Obvious Y-shaped fibers emanating from dMTs were identified at the 1.5-, two-, and three-fold stages.
source: Analyses of cross-sections identified obvious Y-shaped fibers emanating from dMTs at the 1.5-, two-, and three-fold stages (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2.

claim: At the comma stage, shorter fiber-like densities without fully formed Y-link endings extending from subsets of dMTs were observed, potentially representing nascent Y-links.
source: At the comma stage, we observed shorter fiber-like densities without fully formed Y-link endings extending from subsets of dMTs (Figure 1Diii), potentially representing nascent Y-links.
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1, with speculation about their identity.

claim: Structural features of TZs of a subset of amphid sensory neurons are at least partly established by the 1.5-fold stage of embryogenesis.
source: These observations suggest that structural features of TZs of a subset of amphid sensory neurons are at least partly established by the 1.5-fold stage of embryogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the observation of Y-links at the 1.5-fold stage.

claim: Amphid sensory cilia contain a variable number of inner singlet MTs (isMTs) inside adult axonemes.
source: A puzzling feature of amphid sensory cilia is the presence of a variable number of inner singlet MTs (isMTs) inside adult axonemes (Perkins et al., 1986; Doroquez et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: isMTs are smaller in diameter compared to A-tubules of the centriole/BB/axoneme.
source: These isMTs are smaller in diameter compared to A-tubules of the centriole/BB/axoneme and contain 11 protofilaments similar to cytoplasmic MTs in C. elegans (Perkins et al., 1986; Doroquez et al., 2014; Chalfie and Thomson, 1979).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: isMTs contain 11 protofilaments similar to cytoplasmic MTs in C. elegans.
source: These isMTs are smaller in diameter compared to A-tubules of the centriole/BB/axoneme and contain 11 protofilaments similar to cytoplasmic MTs in C. elegans (Perkins et al., 1986; Doroquez et al., 2014; Chalfie and Thomson, 1979).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Only one isMT was observed in one axoneme at the two-fold stage.
source: We defined isMTs as fully closed MTs that were observed inside axonemes over multiple tomographic slices. Using these criteria, we observed only one isMT in one axoneme at the two-fold stage and multiple isMTs in all examined axonemes at the three-fold stage (Figure 2Biv, Ciii and Civ; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Multiple isMTs were observed in all examined axonemes at the three-fold stage.
source: We defined isMTs as fully closed MTs that were observed inside axonemes over multiple tomographic slices. Using these criteria, we observed only one isMT in one axoneme at the two-fold stage and multiple isMTs in all examined axonemes at the three-fold stage (Figure 2Biv, Ciii and Civ; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Incompletely closed MTs and short MT-like structures were detected inside multiple axonemes at the two-fold stage, which may represent early stages of isMT assembly.
source: However, we detected incompletely closed MTs and short MT-like structures inside multiple axonemes at the two-fold stage (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A); these structures may represent early stages of isMT assembly.
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2—figure supplement 3, with speculation about their identity.

claim: A ring-like structure was noted in distal regions of the TZs in two- and three-fold axonemes.
source: We also noted a ring-like structure in distal regions of the TZs in two- and three-fold axonemes (Figure 2Bii–iii, Cii–iii).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 2.

claim: The ring-like structure in distal regions of the TZs is likely the apical ring hypothesized to provide an attachment site for isMTs.
source: This structure is likely the apical ring hypothesized to provide an attachment site for isMTs (Perkins et al., 1986; Doroquez et al., 2014; Blacque and Sanders, 2014).
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the observed structure and prior hypotheses.

claim: The origin and function of the isMTs remain to be determined.
source: The origin and function of the isMTs remain to be determined.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a gap in knowledge.

claim: In a subset of ciliated sensory neurons in the head amphid organs of C. elegans, the outer centriole wall is remodeled to initiate ciliogenesis and persists thereafter into adulthood.
source: Our observations suggest that in a subset of ciliated sensory neurons in the head amphid organs of C. elegans, the outer centriole wall is remodeled to initiate ciliogenesis and persists thereafter into adulthood, while the centriole core degenerates starting at the 1.5-fold embryonic stage (summarized in Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the observations presented in the Results, and is summarized in Figure 3C.

claim: The centriole core degenerates starting at the 1.5-fold embryonic stage in a subset of ciliated sensory neurons in the head amphid organs of C. elegans.
source: Our observations suggest that in a subset of ciliated sensory neurons in the head amphid organs of C. elegans, the outer centriole wall is remodeled to initiate ciliogenesis and persists thereafter into adulthood, while the centriole core degenerates starting at the 1.5-fold embryonic stage (summarized in Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the observations presented in the Results, and is summarized in Figure 3C.

claim: The remodeling of the outer centriole wall is consistent with the persistence of a subset of outer centriole wall- and centriole-associated proteins (eg. HYLS-1 and DYF-19/FBF1) through postembryonic stages.
source: This remodeling is consistent with the persistence of a subset of outer centriole wall- and centriole-associated proteins (eg. HYLS-1 and DYF-19/FBF1) through postembryonic stages (Dammermann et al., 2009; Mohan et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2013, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Amphid channel cilia in adult C. elegans hermaphrodites do not completely lack a BB, but instead possess a modified BB at their base.
source: Thus, amphid channel cilia in adult C. elegans hermaphrodites do not completely lack a BB, but instead possess a modified BB at their base.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the observed persistence of the outer centriole wall.

claim: Proteins (e.g. kinesin-II, DYF-19/FBF1, and HYLS-1) localized to the modified BB region in adult cilia have previously been implicated in loading, ciliary import, and recycling of IFT machinery.
source: Proteins (e.g. kinesin-II, DYF-19/FBF1, and HYLS-1) localized to this region in adult cilia have previously been implicated in loading, ciliary import, and recycling of IFT machinery (Wei et al., 2013, 2016; Prevo et al., 2015), suggesting that this modified BB retains at least a subset of the functions of canonical BBs in other organisms.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The modified BB retains at least a subset of the functions of canonical BBs in other organisms.

claim: Mature centrioles generally contain nine dMTs in the Drosophila embryo.
source: Although mature centrioles generally contain nine dMTs in the Drosophila embryo, centrioles consisting of nine sMTs with lateral hooks have also been observed, and it has been speculated that these structures represent intermediates in the centriole assembly process (Gottardo et al., 2015).

claim: Centrioles consisting of nine sMTs with lateral hooks have been observed in Drosophila embryo, and it has been speculated that these structures represent intermediates in the centriole assembly process.

claim: B-tubules in C. elegans amphid BBs appear to form via closure of A-tubule-associated hooks at the inner AB junction.

claim: B-tubules open at the inner AB junction have been observed in C. elegans mutant for the TZ component NPHP-4.
source: Intriguingly, B-tubules open at the inner AB junction have been observed in C. elegans and mice mutant for the TZ component NPHP-4 and the small GTPase Arl13b, respectively, raising the possibility that these defects may be a consequence of failure to close this junction during development (Jauregui et al., 2008; Caspary et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: B-tubules open at the inner AB junction have been observed in mice mutant for the small GTPase Arl13b.

source: At the 1.5-fold stage, clear Y-links are associated with BBs that either lack or contain the central tube, suggesting that while initiation of Y-link formation may require the centriole core, the core is dispensable for axoneme elongation.

source: At the 1.5-fold stage, clear Y-links are associated with BBs that either lack or contain the central tube, suggesting that while initiation of Y-link formation may require the centriole core, the core is dispensable for axoneme elongation.

source: At the 1.5-fold stage, clear Y-links are associated with BBs that either lack or contain the central tube, suggesting that while initiation of Y-link formation may require the centriole core, the core is dispensable for axoneme elongation.

claim: Eight of the amphid sensory neurons extend their simple rod-like cilia through a channel created by glial cells.
source: Eight of these neurons extend their simple rod-like cilia through a channel created by glial cells (Ward et al., 1975; Perkins et al., 1986; Doroquez et al., 2014) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: Amphid sensory neurons are born over a period of time from the end of ventral closure to the comma stage of embryogenesis.
source: Amphid sensory neurons are born over a period of time from the end of ventral closure to the comma stage of embryogenesis (Sulston et al., 1983) (Figure 1A), and cilia of 3 μm or longer have been previously detected in these neurons starting at the three-fold stage using fluorescent reporters (Fujiwara et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim and is illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Cilia of 3 μm or longer have been previously detected in amphid sensory neurons starting at the three-fold stage using fluorescent reporters.
source: Amphid sensory neurons are born over a period of time from the end of ventral closure to the comma stage of embryogenesis (Sulston et al., 1983) (Figure 1A), and cilia of 3 μm or longer have been previously detected in these neurons starting at the three-fold stage using fluorescent reporters (Fujiwara et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Core centriole proteins such as SAS-4 are not detected at late embryonic developmental times in amphid sensory neurons.
source: However, core centriole proteins such as SAS-4 are not detected at these later developmental times (Dammermann et al., 2009; Schouteden et al., 2015; Kirkham et al., 2003) (Figure 1A), suggesting that the centriole has at least partly degenerated, and that cilia have elongated by these late embryonic stages.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim and is illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The centriole has at least partly degenerated by late embryonic stages in amphid sensory neurons.
source: However, core centriole proteins such as SAS-4 are not detected at these later developmental times (Dammermann et al., 2009; Schouteden et al., 2015; Kirkham et al., 2003) (Figure 1A), suggesting that the centriole has at least partly degenerated, and that cilia have elongated by these late embryonic stages.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the absence of core centriole proteins.

claim: Cilia have elongated by late embryonic stages in amphid sensory neurons.
source: However, core centriole proteins such as SAS-4 are not detected at these later developmental times (Dammermann et al., 2009; Schouteden et al., 2015; Kirkham et al., 2003) (Figure 1A), suggesting that the centriole has at least partly degenerated, and that cilia have elongated by these late embryonic stages.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the detection of long cilia at late stages.

claim: Centrioles comprised of the central tube surrounded by sMTs with hook-like appendages were observed in many cells at 350 mpf.
source: Nevertheless, consistent with previous reports (Pelletier et al., 2006; Delattre et al., 2004; Mikeladze-Dvali et al., 2012), we observed centrioles comprised of the central tube surrounded by sMTs with hook-like appendages in many cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1B, with citations to prior reports.

claim: Amphid channels were unable to be detected in embryos at 350 mpf.
source: Although a subset of amphid neurons has already been born by 350 min post-fertilization (mpf) (Figure 1A), we were unable to detect amphid channels formed by glial cells in embryos of this stage (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), and thus, could not unambiguously distinguish amphid sensory neurons from other cell types.
evidence: This is an observation reported in the Results section and supported by images in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Amphid sensory neurons could not be unambiguously distinguished from other cell types at 350 mpf.
source: Although a subset of amphid neurons has already been born by 350 min post-fertilization (mpf) (Figure 1A), we were unable to detect amphid channels formed by glial cells in embryos of this stage (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), and thus, could not unambiguously distinguish amphid sensory neurons from other cell types.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a limitation of the observations at this stage.
